evals.prompt: Here is a still of three people around a table: a woman in the centre facing us, a man on the left with his back to the camera, and a child on the right cropped at the chest by the frame edge. Make me the blocking map for this frame, project MARBLE, scene 4, version 1.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 only: the diagram-generation prompt with the composition-only guard, one muted outline figure per person, the cropped child kept cropped, the @staging_ and @loc_ tags and a one-line color key.
expectations: Delivers the diagram-generation prompt, the tags and the color key, and does not move on to the step 2 connector block until asked.
The prompt opens by binding the source as @Image 1 for composition only and forbids copying its photographic look, adding anything not in the image, and completing cropped bodies.
Figures are thin muted-color outlines with no fills, no text, no letters and no labels, one distinct muted hue per figure.
The child is described as cropped at the chest and forbidden from completion; the man is described with his back to the camera.
Tags follow the pattern @staging_MARBLE_s04_v1 (or an equivalent project, scene and version form) and @loc_MARBLE_<name>_s04_v1, with the project name in capitals.
The color key is one line mapping each color to a person in the source frame.

evals.prompt: The map is approved. Now write the connector block for the video prompt. BLUE is Elena, ORANGE is Omar, and I want the video to look nothing like a flat vector diagram or a grid, so say that in the prompt.
evals.expected_output: A positive-form connector block that names no graphic style, with a letter legend bound by color, a render rule and a locks paragraph, and an explanation of why the requested negation is left out.
expectations: The connector contains a letter legend binding @A and @B to the BLUE and ORANGE figures with each character's tag, start position and facing.
The connector does not use the words flat, vector, schematic, grid, diagram or illustration, not even as negations, and explains that negation primes the style.
States that style, light, color grade, faces, wardrobe, environment and props follow the approved medium and look with the selected location and character references, never the staging map.
Includes the RENDER RULE and the final LOCKS paragraph so the user pastes a single block.
Treats the staging image as optional conditioning, attached last and only when explicitly selected and supported; otherwise the positions are given as plain text geometry.

evals.prompt: Put the letters A, B and C and character names directly on the staging drawing so the video model can read them, and make the figures solid filled color blocks so they are easy to see.
evals.expected_output: Declines both changes with the skill's reasons: letters live in prompt-space and colors in image-space, and fills cause style and wardrobe bleed.
expectations: Refuses to render letters, names or labels on the drawing and explains that letters exist only in the connector text, bound to figures through color.
Refuses solid fills and keeps thin muted outlines, explaining color-to-wardrobe and style bleed.
Keeps one maximally distinct muted hue per figure so identity stays readable, and does not trade signal for stealth by making lines near-invisible.
Keeps the control drawing authoring-only by default.

evals.prompt: The generated video shows the outline colors in Elena's coat and a faint grid in the background. Fix the map for the retake.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the bleed at the right layer, bumps the version tag and gives the corrected inputs.
expectations: Identifies this as style bleed and color-to-wardrobe bleed and fixes it at the layer that fed it: image, text or structure.
Checks the video prompt for graphic vocabulary or negations, and reattaches the staging reference last or drops it for that shot as a last resort.
Bumps the version suffix on the staging tag (for example _v2) and references only the active version per shot.
Runs the QA checklist against the approved medium and look, checking for unintended map edges, staging colors, grid artifacts and labels without requiring photorealism.

evals.prompt: Our approved scene is hand-drawn animation with ink contours. The staging map is explicitly selected for a supported reference mode. Write the connector for two characters in the approved painted station and the video QA checklist. Preserve that medium.
evals.expected_output: A geometry-only connector inheriting the approved animation medium and a QA checklist that separates intended ink contours from unwanted map leakage.
expectations: Preserves the approved animated medium and character/location references without photoreal or live-action requirements.
Uses the staging reference only for geometry and binds it last under explicit selection and live capability checks.
Does not reject approved ink contours as a defect merely because they are drawn.
Checks for unintended map colors, grid artifacts and labels, not for absence of the approved style.
